sections.label: Youth mental health challenges rise
sections.summary: One in four young people face mental health challenges, compared to one in five in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Notably, one in four young people face mental health challenges, as compared to one in five in 2020.

sections.label: National Mental Health and Well-being Strategy
sections.summary: The National Mental Health and Well-being Strategy was launched by the Inter-agency Taskforce on Mental Health and Well-being in October 2023.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The newly introduced National Mental Health and Well-being Strategy, and henceforth, I will refer to it as “the strategy”, launched by the Inter-agency Taskforce on Mental Health and Well-being in October 2023 is a commendable step forward.

sections.label: Economic cost of depression and anxiety
sections.summary: WHO states depression and anxiety cost the global economy $1 trillion yearly, and a Duke-NUS study found Singapore's cost is $15.7 billion annually.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: According to the World Health Organization (WHO), depression and anxiety alone cost the global economy $1 trillion per year in lost productivity.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In Singapore, a recent Duke-NUS Medical School study found that the economic cost of anxiety and depression is significant, amounting to $15.7 billion annually due to lost productivity and healthcare expenditure.

sections.label: Three strategic shifts in strategy
sections.summary: The Government outlined three strategic shifts in the strategy: a community-based strategy, empowering individuals with knowledge, and fostering inter-disciplinary collaboration.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: To achieve this, the Government outlined three strategic shifts in the strategy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: First, a community-based strategy; second, empowering individuals with knowledge; and third, fostering inter-disciplinary collaboration.

sections.label: Concerns about mental health services
sections.summary: Concerns raised included high costs, long waiting times, insurance coverage challenges, and workplace discrimination fears about being sidelined or overlooked for promotions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Concerns raised ranged from the high costs and long waiting times for mental health services to challenges in insurance coverage for those with mental health conditions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Workplace discrimination emerged as a poignant theme, with individuals expressing fears about being sidelined or overlooked for promotions due to their mental health conditions.

sections.label: Free mental health check proposal
sections.summary: The speaker proposes a buy-one-get-one-free concept giving a free mental health check with every physical health screening, in line with Healthier SG.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In line with the Healthier SG initiative, which already promotes physical health screenings, I propose an innovative, buy-one-get-one-free concept; for every physical health screening, you get a free mental health check.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This dual approach not only emphasises the equal importance of mental health and physical health but also offers a practical win-win solution for early detection and intervention.

sections.label: Mental health impact and time-outs
sections.summary: It states that mental health has physical and psychological impact, no one is immune, and time-outs without stigma must be the way forward.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It is physical and psychological impact and the poignant fact is that no one is immune to it.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Thus, allowing time-outs without stigma must be the way forward for us.

sections.label: Third time triggers counsellor
sections.summary: It states that a person can take it twice, but a third time would automatically flag her case and require a counsellor to intervene.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: We can even allow her to take it twice.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: However, if she takes it the third time, her case would automatically be flagged and a counsellor automatically must intervene.

sections.label: Accusations of lacking piety
sections.summary: It states that individuals with mental health issues are often accused of lacking piety or not praying enough, which blames them and aggravates their condition.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Most of the time, individuals who face mental health issues are accused of lacking in piety or not performing their prayers enough.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Such views not only blame the ones who need help, but it also aggravates their mental health condition.

sections.label: Spirituality and other methods
sections.summary: It states that spirituality can be one aspect of support but cannot be the only solution, and both methods should be employed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: While spirituality can form one aspect of support, it cannot be the only solution for complex mental health issues.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: To me, both are equally important and, in fact, both methods should be employed.

sections.label: Silver Ribbon anniversary attendance
sections.summary: It states that the speaker attended the 18th anniversary of Silver Ribbon, which was set up to combat mental health stigma through better literacy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Coincidentally, last Sunday, I attended the 18th anniversary of Silver Ribbon, which was set up to combat the mental health stigma through better literacy.

sections.label: WHO mental health action plan
sections.summary: It states that 194 member states including Singapore signed the WHO Comprehensive Mental Health Action Plan 2013-2030, which commits them to global targets for transforming mental health.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: One hundred and ninety-four member states, including Singapore, have signed up to the WHO Comprehensive Mental Health Action Plan 2013-2030, which commits us to meet global targets for transforming mental health.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The plan is wide-ranging and includes ensuring that member states strengthen information systems, evidence and research for mental health to better understand the needs of the local population, ensuring that data is disaggregated by sex and age, and reflects the diverse needs of sub-populations.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It calls for early intervention through evidence-based psychosocial and non-farmacological interventions based in the community, avoiding institutionalisation and medicalisation.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While many of these are points echoed in the national health and mental health and well-being strategy as well as in the Government's recently announced push for more community-located delivery of mental health services, I hope that we can also take inspiration from the ethos behind the WHO plan which, I think, is summarised best in the WHO's Constitution itself, and I quote, "Health, is a state of complete physical mental and social well-being and not merely the absence of disease or infirmity." Many of us know instinctively that this definition makes sense and should be what we aim towards as a society.

sections.label: Quality of Life survey decline
sections.summary: Researchers repeated the Quality of Life survey in Singapore in 2022 and found declines in life satisfaction and well-being.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Assoc Prof Siok Kuan Tambyah and other researchers, repeated their Quality of Life survey in Singapore in 2022 and found significant decline in Singaporean's satisfaction of life between 2016 and 2022, and a drop in overall well-being between 2011 and 2022.

sections.label: Diet and depression risk
sections.summary: Some studies found traditional Mediterranean and Japanese diets are linked to a 25% to 35% reduction in depression risk.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For example, some studies have found that individuals on traditional Mediterranean and Japanese diets – which are high in vegetables, fruits, unprocessed grains, fermented foods, fish and seafood – experience a significant reduction in the risk of depression, ranging between 25% and 35%.

sections.label: Sugar labelling and sugar tax
sections.summary: Nutri-Grade sugar level labelling laws are a good start, and a sugar tax should be explored.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Steps to increase awareness of and to reduce our consumption of refined sugars – which are bad for both our physical and mental health in the long-run – through the introduction of the Nutri-Grade sugar level labelling laws are a good start.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We should also explore the possibility of heeding WHO’s calls to implement an effective sugar tax that is equitable and does not punish those on lower incomes.

sections.label: Insurer guidelines for disabilities
sections.summary: Regulators should ensure guidelines prohibit insurers from declining applicants based on disabilities or mental health conditions.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In respect of the upcoming guidelines for insurers to adopt fair and responsible practices towards persons with disabilities and those with mental health conditions, our regulators should ensure that guidelines prohibit insurers from declining applications on the basis of their disabilities or mental health conditions.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Any differential treatment of persons with disabilities and mental health conditions should also be justified by accurate and relevant actuarial or statistical data, and there should be a mechanism by which insurers justify this.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Insurers should also be required to make transparent their grounds for differential treatment or rejection of applications from persons with disabilities or mental health conditions.

sections.label: Safeguards and MediSave mental health
sections.summary: Safeguards like mandatory background checks for those working with children should be established, and MediSave use for mental health services considered.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We should also look to establish safeguards, such as requiring those who work with children to be subject to mandatory background checks, for the protection of vulnerable minors.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I hope that the Government would consider allowing the use of MediSave to access mental health services in other practice settings aside from purely psychiatric settings, particularly in the private sector.

sections.label: Parliamentary Question on insurance stigma
sections.summary: A Parliamentary Question was raised on young Singaporeans facing insurer stigma or being declined coverage for mental health conditions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Last year, on 19 September 2023, I raised a Parliamentary Question to the Minister for Health on what happens when young Singaporeans encounter stigma from insurers or are declined insurance coverage because of a mental health condition.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: This question arose partly from a The Straits Times Forum letter earlier that year – dated 18 July 2023 – where a worried parent, Tan Hui In, shared about how their teenage daughter was turned away by two large insurance companies because of a mental health diagnosis.

sections.label: Insurance premium cliff
sections.summary: It states that instead of a slope of additional premiums based on incremental risks, there is a cliff people fall off when left out of the private insurance market.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In short, instead of a slope of additional premiums based on incremental risks, there is a cliff which people fall off when they are left out from the private insurance market.

sections.label: Regulator reform for insurance
sections.summary: It calls on the Government to get MAS to look at insurance sector improvements and reforms, especially for young Singaporeans with mental health concerns.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: As I said during the 2020 debate on the President's Address, when the invisible hand of the market becomes unbalanced, sometimes we need the visible hand of the regulator to attain the appropriate outcome for our people, in this case, to make sure that insurance companies make decisions which are reasonable and proportionate.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, I call upon this Government to get MAS on board, look at improvements and reforms to the insurance sector, especially for young Singaporeans who may be facing mental health and mental wellness concerns and young Singaporeans who may then be labelled with a diagnosis, with their whole life ahead of them.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Because, Mr Speaker, as I have said before in this House, healthcare is about all our lives – your life and mine.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: And therefore, it is a serious matter when a young Singaporean runs the risk of not being able to get insurance coverage for life.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: And let us all remember, it could happen to anyone of us, or any one of our loved ones.

sections.label: Depression screening for pregnant women
sections.summary: It states pre-COVID-19 depression rates for women and that KKH introduced depression screening for all pregnant women since early last year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Pre-COVID-19, post-natal depression affected one in 14 women, while pre-natal depression affected one in eight women.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Owing to concerns over the rise in the number of pregnant women or new mothers with depression, KK Women's and Children's Hospital (KKH) has introduced depression screening for all pregnant women since early last year.

sections.label: River Valley High School killing
sections.summary: It states the teenager who killed a River Valley High School student was sentenced to 16 years' imprisonment, with major depressive disorder a factor.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Recently, the teenager who killed a River Valley High School student was sentenced to 16 years' imprisonment for his actions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We have learnt through the trial proceedings that his major depressive disorder was one of three major factors that contributed to the killing.

sections.label: Teacher-counsellors deployment target
sections.summary: It states the Minister said MOE aims to deploy more than 1,000 teacher-counsellors in the next few years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Minister also said that MOE aims to deploy more than 1,000 teacher-counsellors in the next few years.

sections.label: Four-day work week option
sections.summary: It states encouraging a four-day work week option for employees with mental health conditions, with pro-rated pay, to reduce stress.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Another way is to encourage the option of four-day work week for employees with mental health conditions to reduce their stress levels and make working more manageable and sustainable.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This can come with a pro-rated pay, just like other part-time employees.

sections.label: Depression factor in murder
sections.summary: The trial showed his major depressive disorder contributed to the murder.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: During the trial, we learnt that his major depressive disorder was one of the contributing factors of the murder.

sections.label: Wage subsidy for mentally ill
sections.summary: The Government is asked to consider wage subsidies so employers hire individuals with mental illness.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Could the Government consider providing wage subsidy to employers to encourage them to hire individuals with mental illness?

sections.label: Senior suicides and depression
sections.summary: A 2022 CNA commentary noted rising senior suicides, a 60% increase for ages 70 to 79, and elderly depression rates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: A 2022 CNA commentary highlighted the rising number of senior suicides.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: There is a 60% increase amongst those aged 70 to 79 from 2021 to 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Around 5.5% of elderly Singaporeans experience depression, as per the Well-being of the Singapore Elderly (WiSE) study.

sections.label: Yio Chu Kang dementia-friendly infrastructure
sections.summary: Yio Chu Kang built Dementia-Friendly Neighbourhood infrastructures from a study of over 100 residents, with two publications for building stakeholders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Last month, Yio Chu Kang implemented several Dementia-Friendly Neighbourhood (DFN)-inclusive infrastructures based on a ground-up and community-based research study.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Adopting an ethnographic research-based approach, the study built on the first-hand feedback gathered from over 100 Yio Chu Kang residents, comprising of persons living with dementia, caregivers and residents, to enhance the neighbourhood to better meet their evolving needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: From the study, several DFN inclusive infrastructures were built and tested across Yio Chu Kang.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This is to enable persons with early to moderate stages of dementia to live and age well in the neighbourhood.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We also launched two publications based on the findings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: These will serve as future references for the building sector stakeholders like the Town Councils, urban planners, architects and designers to build more DFNs nationwide.

sections.label: Incentives for such initiatives
sections.summary: Spurring initiatives like this through incentives or grants is essential.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Spurring initiatives like this through incentives or grants is essential.

sections.label: Flexible roles for older individuals
sections.summary: Reviewing HR systems for flexible roles for older individuals can address manpower, financial independence and purpose.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Reviewing workforce HR systems to enable flexible roles for older individuals can address manpower concerns, instil financial independence and provide a sense of purpose.

sections.label: Economic burden of mental disorders
sections.summary: Studies estimated lost productivity from anxiety and depression at S$15.7 billion and annual mental disorder costs of about $1.7 billion.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As mentioned by the hon Member of Parliament, Dr Wan Rizal, a recent study conducted by Duke-NUS Medical School and IMH estimated the total economic burden of lost productivity due to anxiety and depression in Singapore to be S$15.7 billion.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Singapore Mental Health Study of 2016 also found that the average annual excess cost associated with mental disorders per person was estimated to be close to $4,000 and at a population level, the incremental costs of mental disorders in Singapore is about $1.7 billion per year.

sections.label: Number of psychiatrists
sections.summary: Singapore is estimated to have 4.4 psychiatrists per 100,000 population.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The number of psychiatrists in Singapore is estimated to be 4.4 out of 100,000 per population.

sections.label: Psychiatrist waiting times
sections.summary: Median waiting times for new subsidised psychiatric appointments were 27 days in 2018, 29 days in 2020 and 45 days in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In response to a PQ by former NMP Ms Anthea Ong in January 2020, the median waiting time for new subsidised appointments to see a psychiatrist across public hospitals was 27 days in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The answer to another PQ in 2021 to a question by Mr Leon Perera on waiting times was that the median waiting time for the IMH was 29 days in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Yet, more recently and more alarmingly, in July 2023, to a similar question by the hon Member Mr Yip Hon Weng, the median waiting time for new subsidised psychiatric appointments was 45 days.

sections.label: Initial psychiatric appointment within three months
sections.summary: MOH said 95% of subsidised patients received an initial psychiatric appointment within three months, based on 2022 figures.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Based on another Parliamentary reply in August 2023 to hon Member Ms He Ting Ru on 2022 figures, MOH also responded that 95% of subsidised patients were given an initial psychiatric appointment within three months.

sections.label: Number of clinical psychologists
sections.summary: The list is not exhaustive of all psychologists, and filtering for clinical psychologists gives 292.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This list is by no means exhaustive and indicative of the total number of psychologists in Singapore, as not all psychologists maintain this association with SPS.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, when one filters the search to include only clinical psychologists, the number then whittles down to 292 clinical psychologists only.

sections.label: Subsidies for psychiatric treatment
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to consider greater and wider subsidies for psychotropic medications and other treatments including neuro-stimulation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It will continue to be a moving target, but we must plan forward as specialist resource and infrastructure take time, even years, to come to fruition.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I also urge the Government to consider subsidies of greater quantum and wider coverage for psychotropic medications as well as other treatment modalities, including evidence-based neuro-stimulation treatment, such as repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation as well as electroconvulsive therapy.

sections.label: Measurable targets for mental health strategy
sections.summary: Calls for the Government to set measurable targets for the four focus areas across the Tiered Care Model's four tiers, including reduced waiting times for psychiatrists and psychologists.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In light of this, Mr Speaker, my fourth and final point would be to call for the Government to articulate, as part of its strategic impetus, measurable targets for all four articulated focus areas across the four tiers of its Tiered Care Model for the National Mental Health and Well-being Strategy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For tier 4, at least one cluster of measurable targets I can offer to be met over the next five to seven years would be that the median and 95th percentile of waiting times for access to psychiatrists and psychologists must drop.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I believe that we should articulate a clear target on what is a reasonable waiting time for a patient referred from primary care services to specialist-type services and, in my humble view, I think the last patient referred to a psychiatric service, meaning the 100th percentile, should have access to a psychiatrist, at the very latest, within six weeks for a first visit.

sections.label: Workplace mental health productivity measurements
sections.summary: Cites studies showing absenteeism and productivity gains, returns on workplace adjustment investment, and reduced medical expenses and retraining costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In the realm of productivity measurements, the Asia-Pacific Workplace Mental Health Study by Intellect, a Singapore-based mental health tech company, reveals profound insights.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: It demonstrates how absenteeism and productivity improved significantly – by 4.83% and 6.89% respectively – within just six weeks of active engagements with their services, such as self-help in-app content, personalised coaching and counselling from mental health professionals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: According to the Mental Health Toolkit for Employers, published by the National Council of Social Service (NCSS), every $1 invested in workplace adjustments generates average returns of $5.60, reduces average annual medical expenses by 13.3% and increases the average yearly income per person by 6.5%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Improved levels of employee morale and productivity observed in mental health-friendly companies also reduce retraining and hiring costs, which average $3,650 per employee in Singapore.

sections.label: Singtel iCare programme outcomes
sections.summary: States that Singtel's iCare programme improved job satisfaction, stress management and emotional resilience, with 82% of employees feeling strongly supported.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Another notable example is Singtel's iCare programme, encompassing mental, physical and financial well-being, which resulted in enhanced job satisfaction, stress management and emotional resilience among employees. iCare garnered strong support within months of its launch and 82% of employees felt strongly supported by the organisation and their managers in their overall well-being.

sections.label: Charter signatories' free access benefits
sections.summary: States that the 1,200 and more Charter signatories receive free access to an in-house mental wellness workshop, an advisory session and mental health first aid courses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The 1,200 and more signatories of the Charter are entitled to free access, sponsored by the Charter, to one in-house mental wellness workshop, one advisory session with professional consultants and mental health first aid courses.

sections.label: Government partnership with trade associations
sections.summary: Calls on the Government to partner with trade associations and chambers to implement industry-based mental health frameworks and offer funding through productivity solutions grants schemes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This is an opportunity for the Government to partner with trade associations and chambers (TACs) to contextualise and scale up organisation mental health frameworks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: So, I call on the Government to partner up with our TACs to implement industry-based mental health frameworks and offer funding through productivity solutions grants schemes.

sections.label: Mental wellness in HR competencies
sections.summary: Proposes that MOM work closely with IHRP to refresh its Body of Competencies to include mental wellness aspects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: A significant initial step would be the integration of mental wellness competencies into the existing frameworks for HR professionals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: So, I propose that MOM works closely with IHRP to refresh its Body of Competencies to include these vital mental wellness aspects.

sections.label: CHRO-as-a-service programme proposal
sections.summary: MOM is proposed to deliver services through a CHRO-as-a-service programme to support employers lacking resources to expand HR capacities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: To further support employers who do not have the available resources to expand HR capacities, I propose that MOM deliver services through a CHRO-as-a-service programme.

sections.label: Psychological first aid training objective
sections.summary: Psychological first aid training aims to empower every employee to assist colleagues in distress until professional help or crisis resolution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The primary objective of psychological first aid training is to empower every employee with the knowledge and skills necessary to assist colleagues in distress until they receive professional help or the crisis is resolved.

sections.label: Psychological first aid course funding
sections.summary: Fewer than 10 partially funded psychological or mental health first aid courses appear in a search, so training should be a critical core skill with more providers, funding and a tiered curriculum.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: A search for "psychological/mental health first aid courses" returns less than 10 partially funded results.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Hence, there is a need to include psychological first aid training as a distinct and essential critical core skill, widen the pool of providers and funding for such courses and offer a clearer tiered outline for such training in the curriculum.

sections.label: Aligning Company of Good recognition
sections.summary: Aligning the Company of Good recognition scheme with MOM and WSH Council efforts can create a unified platform.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: By aligning the Company of Good recognition scheme with the MOM and Workplace Safety and Health (WSH) Council’s efforts, we can create a unified platform.

sections.label: Customised organisational mental health framework
sections.summary: A customised organisational mental health framework is offered, supported by the Productivity Solutions Grant for implementing policies, training and programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Three, offer a customised organisational mental health framework supported by the Productivity Solutions Grant for implementation of policies, training, and programmes.

sections.label: Restructuring teams into cell-groups
sections.summary: In response to a tragedy, teams were restructured into smaller cell-groups of 20 to enhance camaraderie.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In response to this tragedy, we took proactive steps to strengthen our community within the company.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We restructured our teams into smaller cell-groups of 20, aiming to enhance camaraderie.

sections.label: Mental health strategy and iWorkHealth tool
sections.summary: The National Mental Health and Well-being Strategy highlights MOM's iWorkHealth tool, and the speaker recommends incentivising more companies to use it and support interventions for workplace stressors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The recent publication of a National Mental Health and Well-being Strategy is a significant step forward.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This strategy highlights the iWorkHealth online tool, developed by MOM and its partners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: My first recommendation is for the Government to look into ways to engage and incentivise more companies to use the tool and support the implementation of suggested interventions to address specific workplace stressors identified in the report.

sections.label: Training HR professionals and managers
sections.summary: The speaker recommends the Government continue supporting companies to train HR professionals and senior managers, working with SHRI and IHRP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: My second recommendation is for the Government to continue supporting companies to train HR professionals and senior managers, working closely with organisations like Singapore Human Resources Institute (SHRI) and IHRP, to build up these capabilities within the HR community.

sections.label: Workplace fairness and resilience
sections.summary: The passage states companies must uphold workplace fairness for locals and foreigners, and warns against both eroding resilience and mistaking resilience for indifference.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Adjacent to this is the principle of workplace fairness, which companies must uphold so that all employees, both locals and foreigners, have a fair and merit-centred basis to chart out their career paths.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We cannot let our focus on mental well-being erode the very resilience that has been the cornerstone of our success.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We do not wish in the long-term, in the name of mental health support, see our competitive edge dulled, our youth's ambition softened by an over-promise of comfort and an under-preparation for challenge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We must build support systems that acknowledge mental health, not as a sign of weakness, but as an aspect of our humanity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But equally, we must guard against a culture where resilience is mistaken for indifference, where perseverance is confused with silent struggling.

sections.label: Youth suicide and mental health data
sections.summary: The passage reports SOS figures on youth suicide, a 2023 NUS study on youth mental health symptoms, and increased demand and wait times for help services.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Samaritans of Singapore (SOS) reported that suicide among youths aged 10 to 29 has gone up, from 94 in 2018 to 125 in 2002; more than 500 young lives lost in the past five years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In a 2023 NUS study, one in three youths reported internalised mental health symptoms, such as depression, anxiety and loneliness, while one in six experienced externalised symptoms like hyperactivity, rule breaking and aggression, while 12% met full diagnostic criteria for having at least one mental health disorder.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The volume of calls and texts for help to social services agencies and suicide hotlines has increased significantly year on year, and residents have told me that it can be very difficult to get through the hotline.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Similarly, as has been mentioned, it takes months to get an appointment at IMH and other hospitals or polyclinics.

sections.label: Girl's school counselling and self-harm
sections.summary: The passage describes a girl who did not want to go to school, found school counselling unhelpful, developed self-harming behaviours and made a suicide attempt.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: She did not want to go to school.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: She saw the school counsellor but did not find the sessions particularly helpful or empathetic. "They were not really focused on me", she said. "Like they would give me study tips when what I needed was someone to help me with my emotions." She developed self-harming behaviours, in part, influenced by her peers, and then made her first suicide attempt.

sections.label: Support plan after psychiatrist and GP
sections.summary: The passage states her support plan, after consultations with a psychiatrist and GP, included exemptions from public speaking and presentations, and extra exam time in a different room.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Her support plan, after consultations with a psychiatrist and general practitioner (GP), included exemptions from public speaking and presentations, and extra time for exams and locations in a different room.

sections.label: C's bipolar disorder and methamphetamine
sections.summary: C took methamphetamine to cope with anxiety, was turned away by IMH and NAMS, and was terminated from his job in mid-2023.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The stresses of his life, in trying to keep his job, trying to get his colleagues, bosses and in-laws to understand his bipolar disorder and the weight gain due to the medications led him to eventually succumb to taking methamphetamine to cope with his anxiety.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: He wanted to stop but, when he sought help, the IMH hotline told him to get help from the National Addictions Management Service (NAMS) for addiction, but NAMS told him they could not help him on his addiction because of his bipolar condition.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In mid-2023, C told his mother he had been terminated from his job as a temporary staff after two months because he could not meet his key performance indicators (KPIs).

sections.label: C's death by hanging
sections.summary: C ended his life by hanging himself in the stairwell of the multistorey car park that evening.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: C ended his life by hanging himself in the stairwell of the multistorey car park that evening.

sections.label: Caregiver mother not asked about coping
sections.summary: She worked multiple jobs to support the family, but no one asked how she, the caregiver, was coping during the doctor and hospital visits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: She worked multiple jobs to support all of them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: But at no time during all the doctor and hospital visits for C, his brother or their father, her ex-husband, did anyone ask her how she, the caregiver, was coping.

sections.label: Strengthening key care settings
sections.summary: The passage asks how key care settings can be further strengthened: families, schools, community, primary care, acute care and online space.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: How can we further strengthen key care settings: (a) families; (b) schools, including universities; (c) community; (d) primary care, (e) acute care; and (f) online space?

sections.label: Consent for children's help
sections.summary: The issue of consent must be addressed so children can get help even if their parents cannot support them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In parallel, the issue of consent is one that will need to be addressed so children can get help even if their parents are not in the right state to support them, and I look forward to details on how the Government will address this.

sections.label: Mental health services in polyclinics and GPs
sections.summary: The Government plans to increase mental health service capacity in polyclinics and GPs, with calls for wider availability, youth settings and a workforce plan.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Government plans to increase the capacity and capability of mental health services in polyclinics and GPs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Wide awareness of the availability of mental health services in polyclinics can help to destigmatise mental health, especially given the stigma around IMH.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I urge the Minister to consider making mental health services available in all polyclinics and not just all new polyclinics.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Anecdotally, although we have a few PCN-MH in Woodlands, only one has made any referrals to our appointed CREST partner.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In the context of youths, we should assess whether youths prefer a different setting from the GP setting, such as specialist youth drop-in centres.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I would also value the Minister's vision for mental health support from GPs under Healthier SG, including whether GPs will perform regular mental health screening and serve as the primary gateway or gatekeeper for referrals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: Across all these settings, we require a robust workforce plan to recruit, train and retain a workforce with experience and competencies in working with young people.

sections.label: Community social workers and frontline workers
sections.summary: The community has many social workers and Malay/Muslim frontline workers like police, SCDF, teachers and nurses who understand mental health.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: Nonetheless, our community possesses certain traits that are helpful.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: We have many social workers within our community.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: We also have many Malay/Muslims who are frontline workers such as Police officers, SCDF officers, teachers and nurses; all of whom would certainly have a good understanding of mental health.

sections.label: Leaders openness about mental health
sections.summary: Leaders can create new openness about mental health by being open about their own personal experiences.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: As leaders, we can help to create a new openness about mental health by being open ourselves about our own personal experiences.

sections.label: LASALLE art and music therapy training
sections.summary: LASALLE has offered a Master's in Art Therapy since 2006, launches Music Therapy in August 2024, with over 177,000 clinical art therapy hours by trainees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: LASALLE College of the Arts, which is now part of the University of the Arts Singapore, has offered a Master's level degree in Art Therapy since 2006.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It will also be launching a Master's programme in Music Therapy come August 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: From a training perspective, this amounts to over 177,000 hours of documented clinical art therapy services provided across Singapore by postgraduate trainees.

sections.label: Greece cultural prescription memorandum
sections.summary: In Greece, a Memorandum of Cooperation for Cultural Prescription was signed between the Ministry of Culture and Sports and the Ministry of Health.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In Greece, a Memorandum of Cooperation for Cultural Prescription has been signed between the Ministry of Culture and Sports and the Ministry of Health.

sections.label: WHO review of arts and health
sections.summary: In 2019 the WHO Evidence Network released a scoping review of over 3,000 studies on the arts' effect on health and well-being.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2019, the WHO Evidence Network released a landmark scoping review of over 3,000 research studies that explore the effect of the arts on health and well-being.

sections.label: Artlift savings in GP consultations
sections.summary: Analysis found a 37% drop in GP consultations and 27% fewer hospital admissions, with a real saving of £216 per patient.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Statistical analysis revealed a remarkable 37% drop in GP consultation rates and a 27% decrease in hospital admissions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: By considering the reduced costs to the NHS in relation to the cost of the Artlift interventions, it was determined that there was a real saving of £216 per patient.

sections.label: Art therapist recognition question
sections.summary: In 2021 the Minister for Health replied to a PQ that art therapy practice need not be legally regulated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2021, when asked in a PQ filed by the hon Member Mr Muhamad Faisal Abdul Manap on whether there are plans to recognise art therapists as allied health professionals, the Minister for Health replied that there was no need to legally regulate the practice of art therapy.

sections.label: Anyone can claim art therapist
sections.summary: In Singapore, anyone can hold themselves out as being an art therapist.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Regardless of this, in Singapore, anyone can hold themselves out as being an art therapist.

sections.label: Queen's University Belfast creatives survey
sections.summary: A Queen's University Belfast survey of nearly 600 creatives found mental health problems three times the general population rate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In a recent research report from Queen's University Belfast, which involved a survey of nearly 600 creatives across a range of artforms, it was found that the likelihood of mental health problems in the arts sector was three times that of the general population.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The most common diagnosed disorders were anxiety at 36% of the group and depression at 32%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This was linked with job precarity in the industry and included factors like erratic and short-term employment, low pay, work-over and under-load, and time away from loved ones.

sections.label: Self-employed arts workforce share
sections.summary: At least one-third of the arts and cultural workforce operates on a self-employed basis.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As we know, at least one-third of the arts and cultural workforce operates on a self-employed basis.

sections.label: National Population Health Survey 2022 mental health
sections.summary: The National Population Health Survey 2022 shows poor mental health rose from 13.4% to 17% between 2020 and 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Several Members of this House have mentioned the concerning data from the National Population Health Survey 2022 which shows that the prevalence of poor mental health has increased significantly between 2020 and 2022 from 13.4% to 17%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: What is of greater concern is the higher proportion of poor mental health among our younger adults aged 18 to 29 at 25.3%, or one in four young adults.

sections.label: Polyclinics providing mental health services
sections.summary: The strategy report states that 17 of the 24 polyclinics today already provide mental health services.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As stated in the strategy report, 17 out of the 24 polyclinics today already provide mental health services.

sections.label: GPs trained under MHGPP
sections.summary: More than 400 GPs have been trained under the Mental Health General Practitioner Partnership Programme since 2012, less than a quarter of about 1,700 GP clinics.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Although it is encouraging to see that since 2012, more than 400 GPs have been trained under the Mental Health General Practitioner Partnership Programme (MHGPP), this is still less than a quarter of about 1,700 GP clinics in Singapore.

sections.label: Collaborative Care Model proposal
sections.summary: The speaker suggests MOH consider approaches such as the US Collaborative Care Model, resourcing private GPs in the MHGPP to include behavioural and counselling therapists.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While I appreciate schemes to make mental health treatment at GP clinics to be more affordable and accessible, such as the CHAS subsidies at CHAS GP clinics under the Chronic Disease Management Programme and MediSave support, I believe that more can be done to enable individuals, who require both medication and counselling therapy in the primary and community setting to get more seamless help.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For example, instead of having the patients navigate a myriad of different professionals for medication and counselling support in different places, would MOH consider adopting approaches, such as Collaborative Care Model in the US, by resourcing private GPs within the MHGPP, to organise their GP-led team to include behavioural therapists and counselling therapists and, focus on providing evidence-based and goal-oriented mental health care for intervention, preferably at designated time or at the convenience of a GP clinic.

sections.label: Relapse risk of mental conditions
sections.summary: Many people are unaware that common mental health conditions such as depression and anxiety have almost 50% chance of a first relapse.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For example, many people are not aware that common mental health conditions, such as depression and anxiety, have almost 50% chance of a first relapse and a higher chance of further episodes of relapses thereafter.

sections.label: Inclusive workplaces and employer education
sections.summary: The speaker proposes the Government leverage the tripartite relationship to work with mental health professionals on understanding and Individual Placement and Support plans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: To enable more inclusive workplaces, appropriate education for employers and co-workers is, thus, crucial.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Hence, I would like to propose for the Government to leverage on the tripartite relationship between employers, the Government and the union to work with the mental health professionals to promulgate more accurate understanding of mental health conditions and some form of Individual Placement and Support (IPS) plans for appropriate accommodation for persons with mental health conditions to integrate and sustain employment for as long as possible?

sections.label: Singaporeans stress levels study
sections.summary: The 2023 Cigna Healthcare Vitality Study reported Singaporeans are more stressed than the global average, with 16% unable to manage their stress loads.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: According to the 2023 Cigna Healthcare Vitality Study, Singaporeans are more stressed than the global average.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: The study also reported that, 16% of Singaporean respondents felt unable to manage their stress loads.

sections.label: Luxembourg right of disconnection
sections.summary: In 2023, Luxembourg amended its labour code to require a right of disconnection outside working hours at company or sector level.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: In 2023, Luxembourg amended its labour code to require that a right of disconnection, outside working hours, must be implemented at the company or sector level.

sections.label: MOM iWorkHealth assessment tool
sections.summary: In March 2021, MOM launched iWorkHealth, a tool to help companies identify common workplace stresses among employees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: In March 2021, MOM launched a new assessment tool, called iWorkHealth, to help companies identify common workplace stresses among employees.

sections.label: NTUC mental well-being course
sections.summary: Young NTUC and NTUC LearningHub jointly developed a course giving peer-to-peer mental well-being support and psychological first-aid skills to distressed colleagues and peers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: To help our youths and young adults deal with stress, Young NTUC and the NTUC LearningHub have jointly developed a course to provide peer-to-peer mental well-being support and psychological first-aid skills to distressed colleagues and peers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Statistics by MOM show that the number of retrenchments in Singapore more than doubled in 2023.

sections.label: Employee Assistance Programme adoption
sections.summary: The speaker hopes for wider adoption of Employee Assistance Programme providers and welcomes Government efforts to subsidise fees of some of these services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I hope that there can be greater support to help with the treatment of workplace mental health challenges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: This can be achieved through a widespread adoption of Employee Assistance Programme (EAP) providers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: EAPs are professionally conducted programmes that are designed to engage employees to deal with their personal and relational difficulties that may impede their work performance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I, therefore, welcome the Government’s current efforts to subsidise the fees of some of these services.

sections.label: Singapore small business owner stress
sections.summary: Singapore's small business owners ranked highest in work-related stress compared with peers in Australia and the UK.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Compared with peers in Australia and the UK, Singapore’s small business owners ranked highest in levels of work-related stress.

sections.label: Private hire driver financial stress
sections.summary: A 2022 IPS study found private hire drivers and food delivery riders reported financial worries, financial stress and declining health.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A 2022 IPS study of private hire drivers and food delivery riders found that 84% worry about not having enough retirement savings, while 88% worry about not being able to cope financially if an accident or serious illness befalls them or a family member.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Unsurprisingly, 94% reported facing moderate to high financial stress.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A significant 44% of private hire vehicle drivers reported that since they started driving, their health has been on the decline.

sections.label: NICA mature freelancer digital support
sections.summary: NICA rolled out digital literacy and skills training during the pandemic, but many mature members struggled, suggesting a need for targeted funding support.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: NTUC’s National Instructors and Coaches Association (NICA) represents freelancers who are instructors teaching sports, arts, exercise or enrichment.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: During the pandemic, NICA was quick to roll out digital literacy and skills training to equip coaches and instructors to conduct virtual classes.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Despite support from NICA, many mature NICA members struggled with the transition.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This suggests a need for the Government to partner bodies, such as NICA, to provide targeted and sustained funding support for mature freelancers to procure and upskill in digital technologies and harness these technologies for productivity and business development.

sections.label: Funding support for mature freelancers
sections.summary: The Government could work with freelancer associations to give mature freelancers sustained funding for upskilling and new software and digital technologies.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Third, the Government could collaborate with freelancer-centred associations to provide mature freelancers with targeted and sustained funding support for upskilling and to procure new software and digital technologies.

sections.label: Mental health issues affect population
sections.summary: Mental health issues affect a wide percentage of the population in varying degrees of severity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Mental health issues affect a wide percentage of our population in varying degrees of severity.

sections.label: Mental health support and treatment gap
sections.summary: Mental health support requires primary healthcare, social, family and caregiving support, and possibly financial support; a Duke-NUS study found a treatment gap of almost 70%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Support for mental health issues require a combination of access to primary healthcare, social support, family support and caregiving.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There may also need to be financial support both for meeting the cost of services and where there is a loss of income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I have been a volunteer in mental health services for about 30 years, and over this period, our mental health services have seen several areas of increasing support with the introduction of more services and also more treatment options.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: A 2022 study by Duke-NUS Medical School revealed that only half of those with anxiety and depressive mental disorders in Singapore were formally diagnosed.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: A lesser 31% sought mental healthcare and still lesser consulted a mental health provider.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: This is a treatment gap, or gap between those who need treatment and those who actually get treated, of almost 70%.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: For the fourth consecutive year, suicide has been the leading cause of death among our 10- to 29-year-olds, and 30% of youths who committed suicide in 2022 were 10- to 17-year-olds.

sections.label: Lowering mental health consent age
sections.summary: The speaker urges lowering the age of consent for mental health services to 18, including interventions requiring medication.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: If our young people are deemed responsible enough to drive as well as bear arms in NS at the age of 18, they should not be held back from accessing mental health services and taking ownership of their mental well-being.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: I urge the lowering of age of consent for mental health services to 18 years old, including interventions requiring medication.

sections.label: Mental health issues among youths
sections.summary: Youths and counsellor friends observed a marked increase in mental health issues and stressors for youths entering Secondary 3, especially females.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Youths and counsellor friends shared observations that there seems to be a marked increase in mental health issues and stressors for youths entering Secondary 3, or the 15-year-olds, especially among the females.

sections.label: Basic mental health assessments in screening
sections.summary: The speaker proposes incorporating basic mental health assessments as part of the annual health screening.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Considering these two available platforms, may I propose for basic mental health assessments to be incorporated as part of the annual health screening?

sections.label: Insurer found at premium
sections.summary: Ms Vas finally found an insurer at a premium of $8,000.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: In Ms Vas' case, she finally found an insurer, at a premium of $8,000.

sections.label: Paid sick leave certification rules
sections.summary: MOM guidelines require certification by a Medical or Dental Registration Act professional, so those seeing psychologists, counsellors and mental health therapists do not qualify for paid medical leave.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Under current MOM guidelines, paid outpatient sick leave requires employees to be certified unfit for work by a medical professional registered under the Medical or Dental Registration Act.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Since only psychiatrists are licensed under the Medical Registration Act, those seeing psychologists, counsellors and mental health therapists will not qualify for paid medical leave.

sections.label: Modifying medical leave for mental health
sections.summary: The speaker submits for consideration modifying the traditional medical leave system to recognise a broader range of mental health interventions, which also provides privacy.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: For individuals seeking mental health support, this also provides a level of privacy.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: I submit for consideration modifying the traditional medical leave system to recognise a broader range of interventions for mental health.

sections.label: Mental health check-ups in screening
sections.summary: Mental health check-ups could be incorporated into national health screening for adults or workplace health screening, and into the National Healthcare Plan.

sentences.text: As with the youths, mental health check-ups could be incorporated as part of the national health screening programme for adults or as part of workplace health screening.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Such a check-up incorporated into our National Healthcare Plan will communicate the importance of mental wellness, encourage conversations and advocate for early help-seeking.

sections.label: Singapore employees most overworked
sections.summary: A 2022 Instant Group study found employees in Singapore are the most overworked in the Asia Pacific, averaging 45 hours per week.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to a study conducted by the Instant Group in 2022, employees in Singapore are the most overworked in the Asia Pacific, clocking an average of 45 hours per week.

sections.label: SMEs employ most of workforce
sections.summary: Over 70% of Singapore's workforce is employed by small and medium enterprises.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the employment landscape, over 70% of Singapore's workforce is employed by small and medium enterprises (SMEs).

sections.label: SME mental health support need
sections.summary: The need for mental health support in SMEs is pressing, and 75% of SME employees see mental wellness as key to well-being.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Regardless, the need for mental health support in SMEs is pressing, and 75% of SME employees believe that mental wellness is a key factor for their overall well-being.

sections.label: Private sector EAP utilisation

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The utilisation rate of Employee Assistance Programmes (EAPs) in the private sector is notoriously poor.

sections.label: Public service officers' mental health support

sentences.text: Could the Government shed light on the support measures and initiatives in place for public service officers' mental health and share data on the percentage of officers who accessed mental health support for each of the years between 2020 and 2023?

sections.label: US disability mental distress study
sections.summary: A US CDC study found adults with disabilities report more mental distress, with 32.9% in 2018 experiencing frequent mental distress.

sentences.text: In the US, a study by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, found that adults with disabilities report experiencing more mental distress than those without disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)

sections.label: UK chronic condition treatment study
