sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A study conducted in the UK shows patients with a chronic physical condition were less likely to have sought treatment for mental health.

sections.label: National strategy for vulnerable residents
sections.summary: It may make sense for the national mental health strategy to include a dedicated approach for vulnerable residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the Singaporean context, while we make mental health a national agenda, it may make sense for the national strategy to also include a dedicated approach to identify and look after the mental health of our more vulnerable residents.

sections.label: Mental illness cost study
sections.summary: A 2023 Duke-NUS and IMH study suggested anxiety and depression could cost Singapore nearly $16 billion yearly from absenteeism, reduced productivity and healthcare resources.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: A 2023 study conducted by Duke-NUS Medical School and IMH suggested that anxiety and depression could be costing Singapore nearly $16 billion a year as a result of absenteeism, reduced productivity and healthcare resources.

sections.label: Poor mental health prevalence
sections.summary: The prevalence of poor mental health rose from 13.4% in 2020 to 17% in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The prevalence of poor mental health rose from 13.4% in 2020 to 17% in 2022.

sections.label: Psychiatrist psychologist waiting times
sections.summary: MOH shared that the median waiting time for a new subsidised appointment was 45 days for a psychiatrist and 42 days for a psychologist.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Last year, MOH shared that the median waiting time for a new subsidised appointment was 45 days to see a psychiatrist and 42 days to see a psychologist.

sections.label: Subsidies for mental illness management
sections.summary: Subsidies for Pioneer Generation, Merdeka Generation and CHAS card holders are up to $540 annually for managing mental illnesses under the Chronic Disease Management Programme for only certain conditions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Subsidies for Pioneer Generation, Merdeka Generation and CHAS card holders are up to $540 annually for the management of mental illnesses under the Chronic Disease Management Programme for only certain conditions.

sections.label: Seniors unwilling to seek help
sections.summary: The National Population Health Survey 2022 found residents least willing to seek help were older adults aged 60 to 74, and seniors' suicide deaths in 2020 hit a 29-year high.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This sentiment is also reflected in the National Population Health Survey 2022, as the proportion of residents least willing to seek help from healthcare professionals or their informal support networks are older adults aged 60 to 74.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This trend is worrying especially as the percentage of seniors' death by suicide in 2020 reached a significant high in 29 years.

sections.label: Seniors living alone
sections.summary: In 2022, 78,600 households were seniors aged 65 and above living alone, double the number 10 years ago and forecasted to rise further.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In 2022, 78,600 households are seniors aged 65 years and above living alone.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This is double the number 10 years ago and the number is forecasted to rise further.

sections.label: Healthier SG mental health services
sections.summary: Healthier SG will include mental health services by training GPs to manage cases and work with communities and hospitals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: On early screening and detection, I am heartened that the Healthier SG exercise will include mental health services by training GPs to manage mental health cases and work with communities and hospitals to meet the needs.

sections.label: Mental well-being commitment and survey data
sections.summary: The Government's mental well-being commitment needs society-wide collaboration, and 2022 survey data shows poor mental health rose from over 13% in 2020 to 17% in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Government's commitment to mental well-being is instrumental in shaping a society where everyone, irrespective of background, can lead fulfilling lives, but this must be amplified by collaborative efforts with non-governmental organisations, philanthropy, the private sector, you and I.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It will take all of society to destigmatise, talking about mental health and normalise health-seeking behaviour.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Some people dismissively say that those dealing with mental health conditions are weak but personally, oftentimes, they are the strongest people I know, for holding on despite the pain.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: To anyone facing a mental health condition and to their loved ones, we see you, we recognise you, you are worthy, and we are so glad that you are here.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Data from the 2022 National Population Health Survey shows that the percentage of Singaporeans with poor mental health has increased from just over 13% in 2020, to 17% in 2022.

sections.label: SOS suicide death figures
sections.summary: SOS data shows 476 deaths by suicide in 2022, up from 452 in 2020 and 397 in 2018, a 20% increase over four years.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Data from the Samaritans of Singapore (SOS) shows that in 2022, there were 476 deaths by suicide, up from 452 in 2020 and 397 in 2018, an increase of 20% over four years.

sections.label: ACEs lifetime prevalence study
sections.summary: In 2020, the Singapore Mental Health Study reported a 64% lifetime prevalence of ACEs among 6,000 adults in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2020, the Singapore Mental Health Study reported that the lifetime prevalence of ACEs in a sample of 6,000 adults living in Singapore, was 64% or, Mr Speaker, two in every three adults.

sections.label: NCSS study on mental health stigma
sections.summary: In 2021, an NCSS national study on societal attitudes towards mental health showed persistent stigma across Singaporean society.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2021, a national study by the National Council of Social Service (NCSS) on societal attitudes towards mental health, showed persistent stigma across Singaporean society.

sections.label: SOS calls from young people
sections.summary: SOS data indicates a 127% increase in calls from young people aged 10 to 19 seeking support.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Data from SOS indicates, that an increasing number of young people are calling their service seeking support, with a 127% increase in calls from young people between 10 and 19 years of age.

sections.label: Unregulated counselling and psychology professions
sections.summary: Counselling and psychology are unregulated in Singapore, so anyone can call themselves a counsellor or psychologist and charge for services.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While Singapore currently offers a world-class suite of post-secondary and tertiary courses in counselling and psychology, neither counselling nor psychology are currently a regulated profession and counsellors and psychologists do not need to be registered to offer services.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This means that, in Singapore, anyone can call themselves a counsellor or a psychologist and charge for their services.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This situation is inconsistent with other developed countries and, as part of the national strategy, I encourage the Government to consider introducing mandatory registration for anyone offering services under the banner of "counsellor" or "psychologist".

sections.label: Mercer report on burnout
sections.summary: A 2022 Mercer report found 85% of employees felt at risk of burnout and almost 50% intended to leave their job within 12 months.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In another report by Mercer, titled the “Rise of the Relatable Organization” released in 2022, it indicated that 85% of employees said that they felt at risk of burnout; and almost 50% said that they intended to leave their job in the next 12 months.

sections.label: National Strategy conclusion on mental illness
sections.summary: The National Strategy is an opportunity for Government to work with private and community sectors to support people who stumble.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To conclude, as we develop this national strategy, it is important to remember that mental illness is not a personal flaw or sign of weakness.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While we cannot live in a protective bubble and completely eradicate all stress and distress from our lives, we do have an obligation to reflect on our society and our culture and to consider how our expectations and the world we have created is making us ill.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The National Strategy is an opportunity for the Government to work hand-in-hand with the private and community sectors to make Singapore a place where we can all thrive and when we stumble, to be picked up and looked after with care and compassion.

sections.label: Speaker sharing personal mental health experience
sections.summary: The speaker became better and felt okay enough to share in Parliament that they had not felt okay not too long ago.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: I became better and I feel okay enough now to be able to make this speech in Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: I decided that I would share in the speech, in Parliament, that I did not feel so okay, not too long ago.

sections.label: Care professionals and family caregivers
sections.summary: Care professionals need care too, and family caregivers in the community bear the brunt of caring for persons with mental health conditions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, the professionals who give care need care too.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: There are more than 100,000 of these professionals that we are envisaging in the national strategy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: The second group of persons who provide care are the laypersons in our community, family members who are caregivers to persons living with mental health conditions in the community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: And in these situations, caregivers bear the brunt.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: I have a resident, who is caregiver to not one but two family members dealing with mental health conditions.

sections.label: Resident charged in Court
sections.summary: Police investigated, Prosecutors reviewed it, and decided to proceed to charge the resident in Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Police came, Police investigated, Prosecutors looked at it and, in the end, decided to proceed to charge my resident in Court.

sections.label: MediShield and MediSave funding
sections.summary: The speaker says MediShield must do more because medications, counselling and therapy cost money, and MediSave500/700 alone is seldom sufficient.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: My hon colleague Dr Tan Wu Meng has spoken about this very eloquently.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: But it must surely be about our universal national healthcare insurance MediShield in the first instance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: MediShield must do more because medications, counselling and therapy, they all cost money.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: And we know that the MediSave500/700 scheme alone is seldom sufficient.

sections.label: Mental health study findings
sections.summary: A study found up to 15% of the sample had poor mental health symptoms, with national productivity and care costs possibly $16 billion yearly, and only a quarter sought professional help.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This study has been referenced already in the debate so far.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It reported that up to 15% of the sample showed symptoms of poor mental health, and when extrapolated to the national level, poor mental health could cost Singapore $16 billion a year in terms of loss in productivity, absenteeism and medical care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Only a quarter of those suffering from mental health conditions in the Duke-NUS Medical School and IMH study sought intervention from a mental health professional.

sections.label: Singapore psychiatrist and psychologist ratios
sections.summary: A 2021 MOH Parliamentary reply stated Singapore has 4.5 psychiatrists and 9.7 psychologists per 100,000 residents, far lower than 280 doctors per 100,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: According to a Parliamentary reply by MOH in 2021, there are 4.5 psychiatrists and 9.7 psychologists per 100,000 residents in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This is far lower than the ratio of 280 doctors to 100,000 residents in Singapore.

sections.label: National Employee Assistance Programmes proposal
sections.summary: The speaker hopes MOM considers a national demand aggregation contract and a pre-selected panel of EAP providers to strengthen adoption of Employee Assistance Programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In a similar vein, I hope that MOM will consider setting up a demand aggregation contract at a national level to strengthen the adoption of Employee Assistance Programmes (EAPs) which are confidential professional assistance programmes designed to help employees manage work and non-work stressors among companies in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: To mitigate the cost and complexities of setting up EAPs by individual companies, I would like MOM to consider pre-selecting a panel of EAP providers for companies to send their employees to.

sections.label: Splitting IMH functions proposal
sections.summary: The speaker suggests MOH consider splitting IMH functions, with a National Mental Wellness Centre for subsidised mental health interventions while IMH handles psychiatric disorders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: To further support the public education on the differences between mental health and mental disorder and to promote help-seeking, I would like to also suggest to MOH to consider splitting the functions of IMH into different institutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Just as we have specialised medical centres like the National Skin Centre, National Heart Centre, National Cancer Centre and so on, can we not have a National Mental Wellness Centre that focuses on subsidised interventions for mental health, while IMH continues to provide medical interventions mainly for psychiatric disorders?

sections.label: Postnatal depression study findings
sections.summary: Studies show about one in 10 women experience postnatal depression within the first three months of giving birth, with those depressed during pregnancy most likely depressed after delivery.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Studies have shown that about one in 10 women experience postnatal depression within the first three months of giving birth, with those who were depressed during pregnancy most likely to be depressed after delivery.

sections.label: KKH postpartum depression screening increase
sections.summary: KKH saw a 47% increase in patients screening positive for postpartum depression between April 2021 and March 2022 compared to the previous year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Between April 2021 and March 2022, KK Women's and Children's Hospital (KKH) has seen a 47% increase in its patients who screened positive for postpartum depression, compared to the same period the previous year.

sections.label: KKH training Punggol Polyclinic nurses
sections.summary: Since 2019, KKH specialists have partnered and trained Punggol Polyclinic nurses on postpartum depression, as part of a SingHealth Polyclinics and Temasek Foundation collaboration.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Since 2019, specialists from KKH have begun to partner and train Punggol Polyclinic nurses, as part of the collaboration between SingHealth Polyclinics and Temasek Foundation to enhance their knowledge on postpartum depression in women.

sections.label: NUS study on peer support
sections.summary: A 2021 NUS Alice Lee Centre for Nursing Studies study revealed peer support can help reduce the risk of mummies developing postpartum depression.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: A study by the NUS Alice Lee Centre for Nursing Studies in 2021 revealed that support from peers can help to reduce the risk of mummies developing postpartum depression.

sections.label: Cookie session on depression signs
sections.summary: In 2022, with Depressed Cake Shop Singapore and SAMH, a cookie decoration session was held at Fuchun Community Club where SAMH shared depression signs and community resources.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In 2022, together with Depressed Cake Shop Singapore and with our community partner, the Singapore Association for Mental Health (SAMH), we organised and invited young parents with their children to attend a cookie decoration session at our Fuchun Communiity Club, in which SAMH shared several signs to identify if one is suffering from depression and the resources available in the community that can be used for support.

sections.label: Husbands depression when mothers depressed
sections.summary: Research shows that when mothers suffer from depression, one out of every two husbands will also suffer from depression.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Research also shows that when mothers suffer from depression, out of every two husbands, one will also suffer from depression.

sections.label: PAP Women's Wing focus group feedback
sections.summary: A PAP Women's Wing focus group with over 60 participants showed consensus that more needs to be done to support new fathers as well as mothers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: During a focus group discussion organised by the PAP Women’s Wing last year, the feedback which we gathered from over 60 participants showed a consensus that, apart from having the need to do more to support mothers, more also needs to be done to support new fathers, as they too may be prone to suffering from depression in silence while trying to support their wives through this challenging period.

sections.label: Corporate measures for fathers
sections.summary: Working with corporate entities to introduce measures letting fathers be caretakers while maintaining a presence at work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Another way to reduce the stress of fathers is to work together with corporate entities to introduce new measures that allow them to play the role of caretaker while still maintaining a presence at work.

sections.label: National Mental Health Strategy launch
sections.summary: MOH launched the National Mental Health and Well-being Strategy in October 2023 focusing on four main areas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The discussion continues as this will be a work-in-progress as we refine our approach and we come to a collective agreement on what we do about it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Hence, I am glad in October 2023, MOH has taken the lead by launching the National Mental Health and Well-being Strategy focusing on four main areas: one, expanding mental health services; two, enhancing early identification and intervention by service providers; three, promoting mental health and well-being; and four, improving mental health in the workplace.

sections.label: MOM data and strategy aims
sections.summary: MOM data shows work stress and mental health discrimination increases; the Strategy aims to address these issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: According to data collected from MOM, one in three employees found it challenging to cope with work demands and pressures or felt exhausted physically or mentally from work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Based on a survey conducted by MOM, there was an increase in the proportion of job seekers who faced discrimination due to mental health conditions, from 2.9% in 2021 to 5% in 2022, as well as an increase in the proportion of employees who felt that they were discriminated at work due to mental health conditions, from 3.2% in 2021 to 4.7% in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The National Mental Health and Well-being Strategy aims to address these issues by improving mental health literacy at work, reducing stigma, supporting the employment of individuals with mental health conditions, customising mental health support according to occupational needs and preventing discrimination through fair employment practices.

sections.label: Upskilling and collective agreement
sections.summary: Discussion continues on encouraging employers to upskill employees and reaching collective agreement towards an inclusive society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Or will it be something where we highly encourage employers to upskill their employees from a SkillsFuture perspective, as suggested by fellow Parliamentarian Mr Edward Chia?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I am glad that our society continues to have this discussion as we refine our approach and come to a collective agreement on what we, as a whole-of-nation; Government, businesses, organisations, communities and individuals, can work together towards our inclusive society.

sections.label: Everyone has mental health
sections.summary: Everyone has mental health, not just mental illness, which one in two Singaporeans consider it to be per an MOH survey.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First of all, we all have mental health.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It is not just mental illness, which is unfortunately what one in two Singaporeans consider it to be, according to a survey by MOH.

sections.label: SkillsFuture funding for mindfulness
sections.summary: Supports colleagues' call for mindfulness, authentic listening and care, recommending extending SkillsFuture funding for such learning.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I support my colleagues, Mr Darryl David, Mr Xie Yao Quan and Assoc Prof Razwana Begum's, call for mindfulness for authentic listening and authentic care, which all fall under social emotional literacy and empathic care.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And hence, I recommend extending SkillsFuture funding for such learning.

sections.label: Mental health awareness gap
sections.summary: Eight in 10 Singaporeans recognise mental health as important, yet less than half actively think about their mental well-being daily.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: How is it that eight in 10 Singaporeans recognise mental health to be important and as important as physical health, yet less than half of us actively think about our mental well-being or how we are feeling on a day-to-day basis?

sections.label: Right to Disconnect proposal
sections.summary: In 2020, Mr Melvin Yong proposed a Right to Disconnect law mandating downtime from work for better mental health.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In 2020, our Parliamentary colleague, Mr Melvin Yong, God bless his heart, proposed a "Right to Disconnect" law mandating downtime from work for better mental health.

sections.label: Depression and anxiety cost
sections.summary: Last year, Duke-NUS Medical School reported depression and anxiety alone could conservatively cost Singapore $16 billion annually.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Last year, Duke-NUS Medical School reported just depression and anxiety alone could conservatively cost Singapore $16 billion annually.

sections.label: National Well-being Office proposal
sections.summary: The speaker recommends the Inter-agency Taskforce become a permanent National Well-being Office under the Prime Minister's Office.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Collaboration is more possible when we are well-regulated in our bodies and minds to allow for better listening and more empathy that then fosters more trust.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This needs to be a whole-of-Government effort and I recommend the current Inter-agency Taskforce to become a permanent National Well-being Office, not under MOH but directly under the Prime Minister’s Office.

sections.label: National Well-being Index
sections.summary: A National Well-being Index adapted from existing Quality of Life surveys would keep the Office accountable for outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: To this end, a National Well-being Index adapted from existing Quality of Life surveys will be helpful to keep this Office's duties on track and accountable for outcomes.

sections.label: 2022 Quality of Life survey
sections.summary: The 2022 Quality of Life survey shows those valuing traditionalism, sustainability and family over material success were more satisfied.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The 2022 Quality of Life survey results show that those who took a more balanced approach to life, valuing traditionalism, sustainability and family relationships over material success were more satisfied than those who valued materialism over these intangible things.

sections.label: Happiness as national objective
sections.summary: It states Singapore's national objectives list happiness ahead of prosperity and progress, meaning overall security and satisfaction, not fleeting emotion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In outlining Singapore's national objectives, it lists "happiness" ahead of "prosperity" and "progress".

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And here, "happiness" can be taken to mean and referred to the overall sense of security and satisfaction that our people feel as Singaporeans, not just happiness as a fleeting emotion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: To improve on this sense of security, let us have the courage to take a pause and the gumption to try a different narrative than scarcity.

sections.label: Wishes for society's wellbeing
sections.summary: The speaker wishes for healthy children, a rested workforce, and by end-2024 more pauses, introspection and emotional awareness for a mentally well society.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I wish to see children and youths who are healthy, strong in their minds and bodies, with curiosity and connection alive in their eyes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I wish to see a workforce that is free from the burden of relentless and unnecessary busyness, rejuvenated and revitalised to have a high sense of ownership in every interaction, because people, who are well-rested, will have sufficient mental and emotional bandwidth to do so.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I hope by the end of 2024, all of us, including us in this Chambers, would have taken enough pauses to introspect and to reconnect within ourselves and to acquire the language for emotional awareness, to be a more emotionally regulated, emotionally secure and mentally well society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Ms Carrie Tan, you would be happy to note that in my former corporate role, I introduced at my workplace, some four to five years ago, that we do not have any meetings on Friday afternoons.

sections.label: Mental health interventions and initiatives
sections.summary: A UN study found about 90% of suicide victims had mental health concerns; MOH cited resilience building, early spotting, help seeking and support initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: A United Nations (UN) study indicated that about 90% of the people who committed suicide had some underlying mental health concerns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In response to the Parliamentary Questions that several other Members of Parliament and I filed on the topic, the Ministry of Health (MOH) indicated that the best interventions were to build mental resilience, spot early indicators, encourage help seeking and support those in crisis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Ministry highlighted several initiatives it had to address this, including Health Promotion Board's (HPB's) MindSG portal, movements by HPB and the National Council of Social Services (NCSS), to encourage people to seek help, components in school curriculum to encourage children to get help and HPB's campaigns for parents to train them to identify signs of mental health issues in their children; and then, once people come forward, there are well-being centres in the community to help people, as well as mental health hotlines.

sections.label: Subsidising professional mental health services
sections.summary: The speaker suggested the Government consider subsidising or providing such professional services under MediSave or MediFund to reduce financial barriers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In a supplementary question I had asked at that time, I suggested that the Government consider subsidising or providing such professional services under the ambit of MediSave or MediFund, so that financial barriers to getting such assistance will also be reduced.

sections.label: Employer-provided mental health programmes
sections.summary: The speaker notes low employer provision, especially in SMEs, and suggests legislation, tripartite framework or an NTUC umbrella programme to widen access.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Where it is provided by employers, there is no additional financial burden to the State; while if the employer is large, the cost of the service can be aggregated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I understand that the provision of such programmes amongst local employers, particularly in the small and medium enterprises (SME) sector, which make up most of our local employers, is very low.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So, I would suggest that the Government consider the best practices in mental health programmes provided by employers in other countries and whether such programmes can be made more widely available in Singapore, say, either through legislation or through the tripartite framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: For example, if small employers may not be individually able to provide such a programme, it may be possible for the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC) to provide, an umbrella programme that SMEs can sign up for and for which they can contribute to.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I think, ultimately, an important aspect of mental health care is making access to professional mental health more affordable and accessible, and both the Government and employers can play an important part in this.

sections.label: Undiagnosed special needs adults
sections.summary: In Punggol Shore, volunteer home visits identified special needs adults, some in their 50s and 60s, undiagnosed and receiving no support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In Punggol Shore, it was through home visits by our volunteers that we had identified special needs adults.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Some were in their 50s and 60s, undiagnosed and received no support for their conditions.

sections.label: Punggol Shore caregiver training programme
sections.summary: Punggol Shore started a training and support programme for grassroots leaders with Caregivers Alliance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In support of families like the Tans, Punggol Shore started a training and support programme for our grassroots leaders in partnership with Caregivers Alliance, a non-profit organisation.

sections.label: Volunteers sew pizza plushie keychains
sections.summary: Volunteers across Punggol Shore communities came together to sew 20,000 pizza plushie keychains for youths.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)

sections.label: Mental health taskforce and national strategy
sections.summary: After the circuit breaker, mental health service use and helpline calls rose, so the COVID-19 Mental Wellness Taskforce was set up, later becoming the Interagency Taskforce on Mental Health and Well-being chaired by Janil Puthucheary, publishing the National Mental Health and Well-being Strategy.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: After the circuit breaker was introduced, we observed an increase in the utilisation of mental health services and more calls to the Institute of Mental Health's (IMH's) mental health helpline.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is why we set up the COVID-19 Mental Wellness Taskforce, which later became the Interagency Taskforce on Mental Health and Well-being, chaired by Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The Taskforce has published the National Mental Health and Well-being Strategy, which sets out concrete plans to plug existing gaps and to strengthen our mental health ecosystem.

sections.label: Increasing mental health service capacity

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Capacity at long-term care facilities will also be increased to provide step-down care for those who need it.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will increase the number of public sector psychiatrists and psychologists by about 30% and 40%, respectively.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will introduce mental health services to all polyclinics and 900 more GP clinics.

sections.label: Accessible and affordable mental health services
sections.summary: The moves aim to reduce waiting times and make mental health services more accessible and closer to individuals, and affordable through Government subsidies and the 3Ms covering all cost-effective mental health treatments.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Through these moves, we aim to reduce waiting times and make mental health services more accessible and closer to where individuals are, be it at homes, schools or workplaces.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We aim to keep mental health services affordable and we will do so through our national healthcare financing framework of Government subsidies and the 3Ms – MediSave, MediShield and Medifund – which will cover all cost-effective mental health treatments.

sections.label: Policy moves for basic needs
sections.summary: The Government is reviewing the education system, narrowing wage gaps and strengthening safety nets so everyone can be assured of basic needs at every life stage.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The Government is making policy moves in this direction by reviewing our education system, narrowing wage gaps and strengthening safety nets, so that everyone can be better assured of their basic needs at every life stage and can have the space to venture forth and be the best version of ourselves.

sections.label: SG Mental Well-being Network partnerships
sections.summary: The SG Mental Well-being Network links groups and volunteers, and the National Mental Health Office will coordinate these partnership efforts more effectively.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Through the SG Mental Well-being Network, we have been linking up with many groups and volunteers to address the diverse needs of our people, be it befriending lonely seniors or providing a safe space for youths to talk about their mental health struggles.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The setting up of the National Mental Health Office will enable us to coordinate these partnership efforts more effectively and to better synergise and maximise our efforts on the ground.

sections.label: Government plans and deliverables

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The Government has set out clear plans and deliverables.

sections.label: Organising services and support
sections.summary: Services and support must be organised so people get help when needed, and a study showed 37% had internalising symptoms while 12% met criteria for a mental disorder.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Furthermore, 6% of the respondents, who previously met the criteria for at least one mental disorder more than a year ago, no longer had the symptoms.

sections.label: Youth mental health campaign and portal
sections.summary: In a survey of 800 youths, 78% were motivated to seek emotional support, and the portal had over four million page views from over two million users.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: As of 31 December 2023, the portal has garnered more than four million page views, from over two million users since its launch in November 2021.

sections.label: YITs, CREST-Youth and CHAT

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)

sections.summary: Eligible patients can get subsidies up to 75%, CHAS and other cardholders up to $540 yearly, and MediSave use at selected clinics.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: For outpatient mental health treatment offered at polyclinics and public specialist outpatient clinics, eligible patients can receive subsidies of up to 75%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Additionally, individuals who hold Community Healthcare Assistance Scheme (CHAS), Pioneer Generation and Merdeka Generation cards are eligible for subsidies of up to $540 per year for mental health conditions, including depression, anxiety disorders, bipolar disorder and schizophrenia under the Chronic Disease Management Programme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Patients can also use up to $500 or $700 from MediSave each year, depending on the complexity of their condition, at selected clinics.

sentences.text: Patients who require inpatient mental health treatment can claim up to $160 per day, capped at 60 days per year, from MediShield Life; and up to $150 per day from MediSave, within an annual MediSave limit of $5,000.

sections.label: No denial due to inability

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: No Singaporean will be denied access to appropriate healthcare due to their inability to pay.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: MOH and MAS will review this issue and consider how insurance coverage for persons with mental health conditions can be improved.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: To meet the anticipated increase in demand for mental health services, the Government aims to increase the number of psychiatrists by about 30% to 260 and the number of psychologists by about 40% to 300, in the public sector by 2030.

sections.label: Raising community provider capability

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: We are, thus, committed to continue to raise the capability and capacity of our community service providers, while monitoring the changes in demand for mental health services to ensure continued adequacy of the manpower required for mental health care.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: We will set up a new National Mental Health Hotline and Text Service by 2025, which will connect callers and texters to the most appropriate support or services to meet their needs.

sentences.text: While first-stop touchpoints are more specialised in delivering mental health services, we also want to equip 1,500 frontline social service professionals with basic mental health capabilities.

sections.label: Practice guide for mental health services
sections.summary: A practice guide aims to launch by end of this year to standardise screening tools, referral workflows, and IT and data sharing guidelines.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: To provide a more seamless experience for those seeking mental health services, the task force brought together professionals from both social service and healthcare sectors to develop a practice guide, which we aim to launch by the end of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: The practice guide will standardise: one, common mental health screening and assessment tools, essentially, common language and tools to help service providers identify their clients' level of mental health needs; two, common collaboration and referral workflows, to guide service providers to determine which service provider to refer their client to, depending on their level of mental health needs and other factors, such as age and cost and how they can collaborate to serve the best interests of the client; and three, common IT system and data sharing guidelines, to streamline referral processes while safeguarding and addressing clients' concerns about confidentiality.

sections.label: First-stop mental health touchpoints

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: These include: first, a number to call or text; second, a comprehensive website for self-help; and third, a place for Singaporeans to seek help.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)

sentences.text: Companies that find four-day work week feasible and workable for their business and employees are free to do so.

sentences.text: On the issue of workplace discrimination, as raised by Dr Wan Rizal and other Members, the upcoming Workplace Fairness Legislation sends a strong signal that there is no place for discrimination against employees and jobseekers with mental health conditions.

sections.label: Four levels of mental health support
sections.summary: The goal is to improve access to care, mitigate unwarranted medicalisation and reduce stigma, with four levels of mental health support.

sentences.text: Our overall goal is to improve access to care and mitigate unwarranted medicalisation and to reduce stigma.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Because not every mental health issue needs to be addressed by a psychiatrist, just as not every medical condition needs to be treated as an inpatient by a specialist.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: So, as has been discussed, there will be four levels of mental health support: from mental health promotion, self-help and peer support at Tier 1, to the most intensive level of care in hospitals and by specialist clinics at Tier 4.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
